chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Salamah, companion of al-Sabiri, from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): The prayer is called to prayer (adhan/iqamah) while I have already prayed, so he said: 'Pray and make it for what was missed.'
And there is no harm for a man to stand alone in the row if the row is crowded.

key_terms.تُقَامُ: The call to prayer or standing for prayer (Iqamah)
key_terms.لِمَا فَاتَ: For what was missed (referring to the congregational aspect or the missed prayer)

ai.seo_question: What should one do if they have already prayed but the congregation prayer begins?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that one who prays individually before the congregation begins should repeat the prayer to join the group, thereby fulfilling the communal obligation while retaining the individual act as a valid compensatory prayer. This ruling underscores the high status of congregational prayer (Salat al-Jama'ah) in Shia jurisprudence, where joining the collective worship takes precedence over maintaining the solitary act. Additionally, the hadith permits a single individual to stand in the prayer row (saff) even if space is tight, affirming that the presence of one person is sufficient to constitute a valid row for the purpose of congregation.
